newsitem.title: FRANCE: Transport strikes still grip French cities.
newsitem.headline: Transport strikes still grip French cities.

text.p: Striking drivers demanding shorter working hours and early retirement disrupted public transport in about 10 French provincial cities on Monday.
Unions said the strike, halting buses trams and underground railways, would go on for a sixth successive day on Tuesday in at least Marseille, Lille, Toulouse, Nice, Toulon and Cannes.

The stoppages, which began with a one-day protest in about 20 major cities last Thursday, have spared Paris where drivers are already entitled to retire at 55. Toulouse in the southwest has been crippled for three weeks.

Strikers are pushing for a working week cut to 35 hours from 39 with no loss of pay, and retirement at 55 instead of 60. They reckon that both measures would help curb record unemployment of 12.7 percent.
